description:
Record ONE lesson this run learned, so the NEXT run — which starts empty — does not relearn it. Log it the moment a tool misleads you AND you find a way through.

You cannot edit or delete earlier lessons; supersede them: `supersedes` takes the `id` of the lesson to replace, from ateam_get_lessons, whose `correction_rule` says when and how. An unknown id is refused (404); a lesson already superseded is refused (409) naming the current one. The server stamps the id and the time.

PROVENANCE: `job_id` and `actor` are usually null (an agent calling this tool sends no x-adas-job-id / x-adas-actor-id): a lesson cannot be traced to its run, nor 'three runs hit this' told from 'one run, three times'. Do not put a job id in `error`; keep it verbatim.

LOG ONLY WHAT YOU OBSERVED, a correction too. Quote the error VERBATIM; never a paraphrase, never a theory about platform internals. A wrong lesson is worse than no lesson: the next run will act on it.

kind='misleading_success': a call REPORTED success while the effect you wanted did not happen — the class a failures-only log cannot hold.

error.description: The VERBATIM error or failed_steps fragment. Not a paraphrase.

kind.description: failure = it errored; surprise = it worked but not as documented; misleading_success = it REPORTED success while the intended effect did not happen

solution_id.description: The solution this lesson belongs to

supersedes.description: The `id` of the lesson this one supersedes, from ateam_get_lessons — see `correction_rule` in its answer

tool.description: The tool that misled you, e.g. "ateam_build_and_run"

worked.description: Did the workaround work? Omit if you never found out — 'unknown' is a real answer

name: ateam_log_lesson
